purpose: Trace accuracy over the electrode count at several amounts of training data, to test whether the best count moves with the data, as a bias-variance balance predicts.
claim_boundary: Exploratory for BCI IV 2a: planned after its electrode-count curve was known. For Lee2019 the predictions were fixed before any of these Lee2019 models was scored on session 2; Lee2019's final-model curve from the replication study was known. Two predictions, no correction for multiplicity. It explains a result; it does not change the frozen 2a configuration.

D1.claim: With half the training data, fewer electrodes gain relative to all of them
D1.contrast: Lee2019: (relevance-16 minus full-62) of fold models (one run) minus the same of final models (both runs), session 2; full-62 from scripts/overfit_study.py

D2.claim: The best electrode count is lower with half the data than with all of it
D2.contrast: Lee2019: the count with the highest mean accuracy over participants among 8, 16, 20, 32, 45 and 62, for fold models against final models (session 2), and a participant bootstrap of that argmax
D2.test: argmax(fold) < argmax(final), in at least 95% of the 10,000 bootstrap resamples

analysis: seeds (and folds) averaged within each participant; 95% participant bootstrap (10,000, seed 690); BCI IV 2a scored on artifact-free session-2 trials, Lee2019 on all session-2 trials
combined_with: scripts/overfit_study.py records for full-22 and relevance-16 (2a), full-62 and relevance-45 (Lee2019) at the same splits
